rv.q: Are the vitality, craftsmanship and musical chops of Ms. Chenoweth and her co-stars enough to turn a rusty time capsule into a transporting time machine? The answer is an unqualified yes only in the first act

But there is an expired sell-by date to this limited run - an inescapable sense that the sunny 1966 trifle by Jerry Bock and Sheldon Harnick got stuck into this big dark theater as filler between more interesting work.
Roundabout’s decision to upgrade to Broadway in a slapped-together production at Studio 54 only exposes the flimsy material's limitations.
So do yourself a favor and fall under The Apple Tree‘s considerable charms.
As a showcase for her dazzling talents, the show is, however, little more than three lame elongated musical skits stretched to the bursting point.
Gary Griffin has directed this revival of a play that premiered 40 years ago with a light comic touch that lets us laugh and take the show seriously at the same time.

cn.t: Chenoweth dazzles in this charming but dated star vehicle, elevating flimsy material through sheer charisma. Critics find the three-part musical a lightweight confection that works best as a showcase for its talented leads.

sg.ra: SeatPlan names Center Orchestra rows E-G as the best seats overall, citing 'a winning mix of perfect proximity and elevated view over the heads in front' on a good rake with a low stage. Headout notes the 'outstanding inclination' keeps sightlines clear from middle rows. AVFMS Row D seat 2: 'Perfect view with unlimited legroom.' 16-row section seats ~350 of the 413 total; low stage means front rows don't require neck strain.

SeatPlan explicitly names Left and Right Mezzanine as 'the best value seats at the Laura Pels Theatre,' citing cheap tickets vs. central Orchestra with 'a clear and close view.' Only 3 rows (AA/BB/CC), under 100 seats — feels intimate and close to stage. Headout confirms 'very little restriction from the Mezzanine overhang at the back' of the Orchestra, meaning the Mezzanine itself is close/low. Row BB flagged by Headout as a specific value row.
